posts.title: My ERP runs Doom
posts.text:
# My ERP runs Doom

I recently joined [Dokos.io](https://dokos.io), which maintains Dodock and
Dokos — French forks of Frappe and of ERPNext respectively. Learning a new
framework means reading a lot of documentation, and documentation only tells
you what the authors thought was worth writing down. So I did the due diligence
any serious engineer owes their employer: I checked whether it runs Doom.

It does. `/doom` on the site, and when you finish a level the run is stored as
a real ERP document.

That last part is the bit I actually enjoyed. Submittable documents are a
framework feature, so this is Frappe — and Dodock downstream of it — rather
than anything the ERP layer adds. A DocType can be *submittable*: a document
starts as a draft, gets submitted, and from then on it is immutable unless you
cancel and amend it. That is the lifecycle of a purchase order. It is now also
the lifecycle of my attempt at E1M1. A run opens as a draft when the level
loads and is submitted when the level ends — through the exit, or face down. It
shows up in the desk UI, it is queryable, it has a permission model. Frappe's
document engine did not notice anything unusual.

## How it fits together

Three layers, none of them exotic.

**The engine.** [DoomGeneric](https://github.com/ozkl/doomgeneric) (pinned at
`dcb7a8d`) compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten. DoomGeneric's whole premise
is that the platform layer is four functions — init, draw frame, sleep, get key
— so the port is a single `doomgeneric_emscripten.c` with no SDL and no sound.
The output is 371 KB of `.wasm`, 70 KB of JS glue and a 27.5 MB preloaded IWAD
— Freedoom Phase 1, since that is the game data this may legally ship.
`DG_DrawFrame` hands JS a pointer to a `0x00RRGGBB` framebuffer, which gets
swizzled into an `ImageData` and painted onto a 640×400 canvas. `main()` drives
the tick with `emscripten_set_main_loop`, no ASYNCIFY, because `TryRunTics`
already yields once a tic has elapsed.

**The bridge.** The game has to tell the ERP what happened. A Python script
injects four `EM_ASM` hooks into the vanilla sources at build time — level
start, live stats, level complete, death. It patches by string
search-and-insert rather than applying a diff, so it survives upstream line
numbers drifting, and it is idempotent. The upstream checkout stays a pristine
submodule; no fork to rebase.

**The app.** A Frappe app with the usual DocTypes (Doom Run, Doom Level, Doom
Monster, Doom Weapon — the schema got ambitious) and a frappe-ui SPA served
from a portal page. Two whitelisted endpoints open and close a run. A
leaderboard aggregates fastest completion and best kill count per level. It
runs on `frappe/erpnext:v15.121.1` with MariaDB and Redis, and — since I had to
know — on `registry.gitlab.com/dokos/dokos:latest`, Dodock 5.16.5, by changing
the base image line and nothing else. The site installs the app alone, never
the ERP one, so both stacks exercise the framework by itself.

## Things that were not obvious

**Attract mode will fill your database.** The obvious place to detect the start
of a level is `G_DoLoadLevel`. Do that and every idle title screen quietly
opens a run, because `G_DoPlayDemo` calls `G_InitNew` — which loads the level
*and* clears `demoplayback` — and only sets `demoplayback = true` after it
returns. Inside `G_DoLoadLevel` the flag reads false even for the built-in
demos. The fix is to test `(levelstarttic, gamemap)` once per tic in `G_Ticker`
instead, where the flag has settled.

**Doom 1 has no GAME OVER screen.** I went looking for one to hook. The string
does not exist in the source. In single player, dying routes through
`G_DoReborn`, which sets `gameaction = ga_loadlevel` and restarts the map. That
reload is also what opens the next run, which turned out to be convenient.

**`i_input.c` must stay in the build.** It looks like an input backend you can
drop along with the SDL files. It defines `I_GetEvent`, the only consumer of
`DG_GetKey`. Remove it and the game runs perfectly while ignoring the keyboard
completely.

**`HEAPU32` has to be exported explicitly**, and re-read every frame — the
typed array view is replaced when memory grows, so a cached reference silently
starts pointing at nothing.

## The actual point

The joke writes itself, but the reason this took an evening rather than a
fortnight is worth saying plainly. Frappe gives you a document model with
drafts, submission, permissions and an admin UI more or less for free, and a
portal page is just a route where you can serve whatever you want. I did not
fight the framework once. The only genuinely hard parts were in 1993 C code and
in Emscripten's memory model — which is exactly the right place for the hard
parts to be.

Frappe is a good framework, and so is Dodock downstream of it. Now I have a
benchmark to prove it.

---

*The engine is DoomGeneric compiled to WebAssembly and is GPL-2.0; the
corresponding source and the exact build script are in the repository. Game
data is [Freedoom](https://freedoom.github.io/) Phase 1, BSD 3-clause — id
Software's shareware WAD is deliberately not shipped, since its licence covers
redistributing the complete shareware package rather than a lone IWAD served
over HTTP. If you own Doom, `IWAD=doom1.wad ./build.sh` uses it locally. Not
affiliated with id Software.*
